audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] reads Pantheon while the late paragraph opens 'By 2 items this is his lane' and whys[6] says 'By 2+ items he out-scales decisively'.
audit.why: Two strings in the entry and a 49.53% win rate over 1587 games all point the other way, and the packet's levelChart for this pairing gives Wukong the two-item row.
audit.corrected: content win[6] moved from Pantheon to Wukong.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and 'his clone trick' is dismissed as something that does not matter.
audit.why: Warrior Trickster is 22s at rank 1 — one of the longest escape cooldowns in the top lane, and it makes him invisible as well as leaving the clone. Nimbus Strike is 10s at 650, Crushing Blow 8s, Cyclone 130s. 'Watch his E-dash' becomes usable once the player knows it returns every 10 seconds while his escape takes 22.
audit.corrected: Written into early, wants.foe[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'watch his E-dash, since he'll try to dodge your W or jump on you after you've committed' conflates two different abilities.
audit.why: Riot: Nimbus Strike (E) 'dashes to a targeted enemy' — that is the engage, it cannot be used to dodge away. Warrior Trickster (W) 'becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone' — that is the dodge, and the invisibility is the part the entry never mentions while telling the player his clone 'doesn't matter in a short trade'. Getting these the wrong way round means holding your stun for the wrong cast.
audit.corrected: Nimbus Strike named as the dash in, Warrior Trickster as the invisible dash out with its 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stone Skin is never named, and Crushing Blow's auto reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot: Stone Skin gives 'stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting champions', so the longer a trade runs the worse it gets for a lethality Pantheon — that is the actual reason to keep trades short, and the entry gives no reason at all. Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset (flagged in _missing-interactions for this pairing), so the wind-up is the step-back cue rather than the cast.
audit.corrected: Stone Skin written into whys[0], whys[3], whys[6], spikes[0], spikes[3], mid, late and wants.you[1]; Crushing Blow's reset into mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says Cyclone's knock-up cancels Aegis Assault.
audit.why: Cyclone knocks up, and Aegis Assault is a channel. The entry already warns that his ult flips your all-in; the mechanism is that it also removes the tool you were relying on to survive it.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright'.
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will. Wukong's passive is Stone Skin, also unnamed until now.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. Wukong has weak base stats and no clone trick that matters in a short trade, so your point-and-click W-stun into empowered-Q burst out-damages anything he can do back. At 2-3 force the all-in — but watch his E-dash, since he'll try to dodge your W or jump on you after you've committed it. Don't chase the W clone decoy; it's a juke to bait your cooldowns.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. Wukong has weak base stats and Warrior Trickster is 22 seconds at rank 1, so your point-and-click W-stun into empowered-Q burst out-damages anything he does back. At 2-3 force the all-in — but know the slots: Nimbus Strike (E, 10s, 650) is the dash onto you, while Warrior Trickster is the invisible dash away that leaves the clone. Don't chase the clone.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 even out. You still poke with the held long-range Q and block his Q armor-shred and autos with E's directional channel, but his sustain damage and item start stabilizing the lane. At 6 his R spin knockup is the real danger — if you W in and he ults, his combo flips your all-in, so don't dive a full-resource Wukong without flash. This is your last window to convert tempo into a Starfall roam before he scales.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 even out. You still poke with the thrown Comet Spear, but Stone Skin stacks armour and health regen on him through every extended trade, so keep yours short and reset. Crushing Blow is an auto reset that also shreds your armour — the wind-up is your cue, not the cast. At 6 Cyclone's knock-up is the real danger: it flips your all-in and cancels Aegis Assault, so don't dive a full Wukong without Flash.

edits.before: By 2 items this is his lane. Wukong's Q armor-shred plus bruiser items chew through your squishy frame while your damage flatlines, and his R knockup makes every extended fight a coinflip you lose. You have no innate sustain to grind it out. Your only path is to have already snowballed — kills, plates, a roam lead — so the late game never happens on even footing. If it's even at 2 items, you're behind.
edits.after: By 2 items this is his lane. Crushing Blow shreds your armour while Stone Skin stacks his own through the fight, and Cyclone's knock-up makes every extended fight a coinflip you lose. You have no innate sustain to grind it out. Your only path is to have already snowballed — kills, plates, a roam lead — so the late game never happens on even footing. If it is even at 2 items, you are behind.

notes: Wukong's two dashes are conflated: 'watch his E-dash, since he'll try to dodge your W or jump on you after you've committed'. Nimbus Strike (E, 10s, 650) dashes TO a target — it is only ever an engage and cannot dodge anything. Warrior Trickster (W, 22s at rank 1) is the dodge, and the entry dismisses it as a 'clone trick that doesn't matter in a short trade' while never mentioning that it also turns him invisible. Those are two different cooldowns with a twelve-second gap between them, and the player needs to know which one their stun is being held for. The other gap is Stone Skin, unnamed anywhere: it gives stacking armour and health regeneration while he fights champions, which is the actual reason a lethality Pantheon must keep trades short — the page says to keep them short in places but never says why. Added Crushing Blow's auto reset (flagged in _missing-interactions) so the wind-up reads as the step-back cue, and the fact that Cyclone's knock-up cancels Aegis Assault, which is the mechanism behind the level-6 warning the page already gives.
